newsitem.title: USA: Lyricist Irving Caesar dies in New York at age 101.
newsitem.headline: Lyricist Irving Caesar dies in New York at age 101.

text.p: Irving Caesar, who wrote the lyrics to such classic American songs as "Swanee" and "Tea for Two," has died in New York at the age of 101, a spokesman for Mount Sinai Hospital said on Tuesday.
The spokesman, Mel Granick, declined to comment on the cause of death.
Caesar, who grew up in the Jewish slums of New York's Lower East Side, wrote the words for about 2,200 songs.

His first big hit -- for which George Gershwin, another product of the ghetto, wrote the music -- was "Swanee" in 1919. The song flopped as part of a Broadway revue but soon became a hit when Al Jolson included it in one of his shows.
In 1932 composer Vincent Youmans "dragged (Caesar) out of bed" to play him the melody of "Tea for Two."
"I made up the chorus ... just as a kind of dummy lyric," the writer, who was known for his speed and skill, remembered on the eve of his 95th birthday.
"After I finished -- which took about five minutes -- I said to Vincent, 'It stinks -- I'll write you something better tomorrow,' he said.
"But he loved it, and he was right; it's one of the most frequently sung and recorded tunes ever written."
